summary:
This bill provides appropriations for the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and related agencies for fiscal year 2024, ending September 30, 2024. It sets funding levels, authorizes programs, and imposes numerous policy restrictions across these agencies.

For the Department of Labor, the bill provides $2,836,808,000 for Training and Employment Services, including $1,807,553,000 for state grants under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and $1,029,255,000 for national programs such as apprenticeships ($285,000,000), ex-offender activities ($115,000,000), and YouthBuild ($105,000,000).

For the Department of Health and Human Services, the bill appropriates $402,341,000 for General Departmental Management, with set-asides including $40,000,000 for competitive sexual risk avoidance grants and $28,000,000 for minority AIDS prevention. The Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology receives $56,238,000. The bill rescinds $1,000,000,000 from the Nonrecurring Expenses Fund, while allowing up to $85,000,000 to be transferred to CDC Buildings and Facilities. It also rescinds $243,000,000 in unobligated balances from the National Service Trust.

The legislation contains extensive policy riders. It prohibits funding for research using human fetal tissue from induced abortion, bars funds to entities that perform or fund abortions (with exceptions for rape, incest, or life endangerment), and blocks funding for a specific organization, EcoHealth Alliance, Inc. It prohibits implementation of the CMS staff vaccination rule, enforcement of Executive Order 13988 on gender identity discrimination, and finalization of a proposed rule on nondiscrimination in health programs. The bill creates a new private right of action for violations of certain funding conditions. It also maintains a requirement that breast cancer screening recommendations reference pre-2009 guidelines through January 1, 2025.

For the Department of Education, major appropriations include $13,055,290,000 for Education for the Disadvantaged, $15,453,264,000 for Special Education under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, and $22,475,352,000 for Student Financial Assistance, setting the maximum Pell Grant at $6,335 for the 2024-2025 award year. The bill rescinds $8,671,399,000 from prior-year Education for the Disadvantaged funds and $1,681,441,000 from School Improvement Programs. Policy provisions block funding to implement or enforce student loan payment suspensions, debt discharge, a proposed income-driven repayment rule, or a borrower defense final rule. The bill also prohibits finalizing proposed Title IX rules related to athletic eligibility.

Other agency funding includes $200,000,000 for the National Labor Relations Board, $11,951,978,000 for Social Security Administration administrative expenses (with an additional $1,851,000,000 for program integrity work), and $593,347,000 for the Corporation for National and Community Service operating expenses. The bill extends Performance Partnership Pilot authority to September 30, 2028, and makes $13,493,000,000 in the Child Enrollment Contingency Fund unavailable for obligation.
